text: I hate times tables. I keep getting 7 times 8 wrong.
I hear you, Diego — 7 times 8 trips a lot of people up. Let's make it easier instead of memorizing it cold. Do you already know 7 times 4?
Nice. 7 times 8 is just double 7 times 4, because 8 is two 4s. So what's 28 doubled?
56. Wait is that it? That felt too easy.
That's it — 56! Easy is good. Breaking a hard fact into ones you already know is exactly what strong math students do. Want a trick to double-check it a different way?
7 times 8 and 8 times 7 are the same — order doesn't change the answer. So you only ever have to learn each fact once. Try 6 times 9 for me, and break it up however feels easy.
6 times 9... I don't know that one either. This is why I give up.
Hey, don't give up — you just nailed a harder one. Let's use the same idea: 6 times 9 is 6 times 10 minus 6. What's 6 times 10?
54 — yes! See, you're not bad at this at all; you just needed a strategy instead of raw memorizing. How are you feeling now?
Better. Can we do a couple more so I remember the trick?
Absolutely — that's a great instinct. Let's do 8 times 9 and 7 times 6 next, using the same break-it-down moves.
